studies.Reference: A case-control study of diet and prostate cancer.
studies.Authors: Key TJ, Silcocks PB, Davey GK, Appleby PN, Bishop DT
studies.comparison_type: top third of intake versus reference third
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Among 13 other nutrients examined, the odds ratios in the top third of intake were below 0.8 for: potassium, 0.74 (0.51-1.09; P for trend = 0.054)

sample_size.excerpt: We interviewed 328 men diagnosed with prostate cancer before the age of 75 years and 328 age-matched population controls.
sample_size.location: Abstract, sentence 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 328 + 328 = 656

cases.excerpt: We interviewed 328 men diagnosed with prostate cancer before the age of 75 years and 328 age-matched population controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Among 13 other nutrients examined, the odds ratios in the top third of intake were below 0.8 for: potassium, 0.74 (0.51-1.09; P for trend = 0.054); zinc, 0.73 (0.49-1.08; P for trend = 0.126); iodine, 0.75 (0.51-1.11; P for trend = 0.077); vitamin B6 food only, 0.77 (0.53-1.12; P for trend = 0.077); and vitamin B6 including supplements, 0.70 (0.48-1.03; P for trend = 0.029). Among 18 foods examined, statistically significant associations were observed for: garlic as food, > or = 2/week vs never, 0.56 (0.33-0.93); garlic including supplements, > or = 2/week vs never, 0.60 (0.37-0.96); baked beans, > or = 2/week vs < 1/month, 0.57 (0.34-0.95); and garden peas, > or = 5/week vs < or = 3/month, 0.35 (0.13-0.91).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among 13 other nutrients examined, the odds ratios in the top third of intake were below 0.8 for: potassium, 0.74 (0.51-1.09; P for trend = 0.054); zinc, 0.73 (0.49-1.08; P for trend = 0.126); iodine, 0.75 (0.51-1.11; P for trend = 0.077); vitamin B6 food only, 0.77 (0.53-1.12; P for trend = 0.077); and vitamin B6 including supplements, 0.70 (0.48-1.03; P for trend = 0.029).
